project: FL-IDS: Making Federated Learning More Secure and More Private
description: Application-layer intrusion detection model (Model 2 of the dual-model FL-IDS architecture). Detects stealth and payload-based attacks via HTTP/MQTT/application features. This baseline uses NO Byzantine attack, NO defenses (Krum/DP/HE/ZKP all disabled), NO learning-rate decay, and NO EMA smoothing — plain FedProx only.

correctness_prerequisites.description: This run is only valid because of three prior fixes to the data pipeline, in addition to the two shared with the network model (see manifest_network_baseline.json for the label-mapping bug and majority-class-cap correction, both of which apply identically here). This section covers the application-model-specific fix.

silently_zeroed_text_columns.root_cause: pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce') silently turns every string-valued column except Attack_type into NaN, which nan_to_num then zeros out. This destroyed all signal in http.file_data, http.request.uri.query, http.referer, http.request.full_uri, tcp.payload, and http.request.method — five columns central to distinguishing SQL_injection, XSS, Uploading, Password, and Backdoor.
silently_zeroed_text_columns.diagnostic_evidence: check_feature_signal.py (mutual information + RandomForest importance on the full corrected dataset) confirmed tcp_payload_len/entropy rank in the top 10 of 91 features. inspect_weak_class_payloads.py showed real attack signal in raw samples: a Password-labeled row's User-Agent was literally 'Mozilla/5.0 (Hydra)' (a known brute-force tool), an XSS-labeled row had User-Agent '--reverse-check'.
silently_zeroed_text_columns.fix: engineer_text_features() in data_loader.py extracts numeric features (length, Shannon entropy, keyword-match flags, one-hot HTTP method, User-Agent tool-fingerprint detection, coarse URI category keywords) from these columns BEFORE the generic pd.to_numeric coercion runs, so real signal survives instead of being zeroed.

dataset.source: Edge-IIoTset DNN subset (DNN-EdgeIIoT-dataset.csv, ~1.2GB, 2,219,201 raw rows, 63 raw columns)
dataset.cap_methodology: VARS-FL (arXiv 2605.05896, Section IV-A): cap the true majority class (Normal) to 18% of the post-cap total — see manifest_network_baseline.json for why this target was corrected from the original (incorrect) 'DDoS_TCP' assumption.

class_definition.imbalance_ratio: Normal:Fingerprinting is ~132:1 — far more severe than originally documented under the (buggy) pre-fix pipeline, which reported a much milder apparent ratio due to mislabeled class assignment.
class_definition.note: Fingerprinting (1,001) and Uploading/XSS (moderate counts but historically weak F1) are the classes of primary interest for this model's known_limitations below.

preprocessing.feature_selection_method: NO VarianceThreshold (deliberately different from the network model) — HTTP/application features have low variance across the FULL dataset but are the primary discriminative signal for THIS model's classes

feature_count_breakdown.text_stat_features: 25 columns — length, Shannon entropy, SQLi/XSS keyword flags, special-char count, computed for tcp.payload (hex-decoded first), http.request.full_uri, http.request.uri.query, http.file_data, http.referer
feature_count_breakdown.user_agent_features: 3 columns — ua_len, ua_non_browser (generalizable: any non-standard-browser User-Agent), ua_known_attack_tool (narrower: named pentest tool signatures e.g. Hydra, sqlmap, Nikto)
feature_count_breakdown.uri_keyword_buckets: 5 columns — coarse semantic categories (xss, sqli, upload, login, admin) matched against combined URI text, deliberately NOT exact DVWA path matching to reduce overfitting to this specific testbed

preprocessing.scaling: StandardScaler (zero mean, unit variance), fit after class capping and feature engineering
known_dead_weight_features: http_referer_has_sqli, http_referer_has_xss, http_referer_special_char_count (all near-zero on both metrics)
method_PUT, method_HEAD, method_OPTIONS, method_OTHER (0.00000 RF importance — these methods are essentially absent or uniform across classes in this traffic)
uri_kw_xss (rank 91/91 RF importance — literally last of all features, despite being built specifically for XSS; the raw-sample XSS keyword hypothesis did not hold at full-dataset scale)
preprocessing.feature_signal_validation: Confirmed via check_feature_signal.py (mutual information + RandomForest importance on the FULL 335,820-row dataset, not a sample). Engineered features contribute 12.5% of total RandomForest importance mass despite being only 43/91 columns — modest in aggregate but with large class-specific effects not visible in the aggregate number (see known_limitations).

layers: Conv1d(1, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1) -> BatchNorm1d(64) -> ReLU -> MaxPool1d(2)
Conv1d(64, 128, kernel_size=3, padding=1) -> BatchNorm1d(128) -> ReLU -> MaxPool1d(2)
LSTM(input=128 [computed via dummy forward pass], hidden=64, num_layers=1, batch_first=True)

loss_function.gamma_history: Originally 3.0, dropped to 2.0 (matching the network model) — 3.0 was tuned under a much milder apparent imbalance (before the label-mapping fix revealed the true ~132:1 ratio) and was found to be too aggressive against the real imbalance.
loss_function.class_weighting: inverse-sqrt of live class counts (get_class_counts_application()), floor-clamped, plus manual per-class boosts
loss_function.clamping_status: FLOOR-ONLY clamp active for this run: torch.clamp(w, min=w.max()/5.0) — raises the minimum weight so the max:min ratio never exceeds 5:1, but does NOT cap the ceiling. This is an earlier, incomplete version of the weight-clamp fix; a later two-sided version (min_mult=0.3, max_mult=2.5 of the mean) exists in task.py but was not active for this specific baseline run.

manual_overrides.history: These multipliers were re-derived AFTER the label-mapping fix, tuned against a real (trustworthy) baseline run's actual weak classes. An earlier set of overrides (Backdoor x5.0, XSS x4.0, Password x3.0, Fingerprinting x3.0, Port_Scanning x1.5) had been tuned while the label bug was still active — those numbers were meaningless once labels were corrected and were discarded, not reused.
manual_overrides.caveat: These specific multiplier VALUES (1.3/1.5/1.3) have not been re-tuned since the newest feature set (90 features) was introduced — they were carried over from the 73-feature baseline. Re-validate against this run's actual per-class F1 before trusting them as final.

federated_learning_config.learning_rate_schedule: NONE — static learning rate across all 25 rounds
federated_learning_config.optimizer: Adam, recreated fresh every client every round
federated_learning_config.within_round_lr_schedule: torch.optim.lr_scheduler.StepLR(step_size=3, gamma=0.95) — applied WITHIN each round's 5 local epochs only, resets every round
federated_learning_config.aggregation: FedProx (weighted FedAvg with proximal term in client loss)
federated_learning_config.prox_mu_history: 0.1 (too slow to converge, still climbing at round 25 in an earlier test) -> 0.01 (severe oscillation, e.g. one test showed round-to-round F1-Macro swings of +/-0.2-0.3) -> 0.02 (this run — moderate middle ground, still shows real but less severe round-to-round variance, see round_25_context below)
federated_learning_config.partitioning: Dirichlet non-IID, alpha=0.7, seed=42, across 10 clients

metric_definitions.f1_macro: unweighted mean of per-class F1 across all 8 classes, computed here from the MEAN row of the per-round CSV log

best_round.selection_criterion: best accuracy AND best F1-Macro simultaneously across all 25 rounds
best_round.IMPORTANT_CAVEAT: Same limitation as the network model — round 20's actual trained weights were overwritten by rounds 21-25 before being saved separately. checkpoint_application.npz on disk holds round 25's weights only, not round 20's.

known_limitations: XSS is the weakest class throughout the entire run, peaking at only F1=0.4518 (round 21) and often in the 0.15-0.35 range — despite a 1.5x manual weight boost. A confusion-matrix diagnosis on an earlier (73-feature, pre-User-Agent-features) checkpoint found XSS's dominant error was 'predicted as Normal' (63.9% of true XSS rows), NOT confusion with other HTTP attacks as originally hypothesized in project notes. This has not been re-diagnosed against the current 90-feature model.
Password similarly weak, peaking around F1=0.56 (round 23). Earlier confusion-matrix diagnosis found 30.3% of true Password predicted as Normal, 23.6% as SQL_injection.

uri_kw_xss — the feature specifically engineered to catch XSS attacks via URL keyword matching — ranked DEAD LAST (91st of 91 features) in RandomForest importance on the full dataset, despite raw-sample inspection suggesting URL-path signal should be present. This is a genuine negative result, not yet explained.
Class weight clamping is FLOOR-ONLY for this run (does not cap the ceiling) — see loss_function.clamping_status. A two-sided clamp exists in a later task.py revision but was not active here.

The manual weight-boost multipliers (Uploading x1.3, XSS x1.5, Fingerprinting x1.3) were tuned against the PREVIOUS 73-feature baseline and have not been re-validated against this 90-feature run's actual per-class F1.
Round-to-round F1-Macro variance is substantial in the first 9 rounds especially (e.g. round 9 dips to 0.517 after round 8's 0.569) — no LR decay or EMA smoothing is active in this baseline.
The 'best round' (20) is a NUMBER only — its actual model weights are not currently recoverable from disk (see best_round.IMPORTANT_CAVEAT above).

9 of the 90 features (http_request_full_uri_has_xss, http_request_uri_query_has_xss, http_referer_has_sqli, http_referer_has_xss, http_referer_special_char_count, method_PUT, method_HEAD, method_OPTIONS, method_OTHER) are confirmed dead weight on both MI and RandomForest importance metrics — candidates for removal in a future feature-set revision, not yet acted on.

uri_kw_* and ua_known_attack_tool features are acknowledged to be dataset-coupled to varying degrees (this is a DVWA-based capture; URL path keywords partially reflect DVWA's own page-naming convention rather than universal attack signatures) — documented explicitly as an external validity caveat for any paper claims based on these features.

reproducibility.framework: custom Python simulation (direct, parallel client training via ProcessPoolExecutor)
reproducibility.experiment_config_json: experiment_config_application.json (auto-generated by main.py at run start, contains the exact runtime flag values)
